title: Protostellar Cores in Sagittarius B2 N and M
question: Resolve protostellar cores in Sgr B2 N and M at ~500-700 AU, establish their nature and evolutionary stage (Stage 0/I YSOs), and derive lower-limit core masses, the core mass function, inferred stellar mass and star formation rate

data.bands: Band 3 and Band 6 (3 mm and 1 mm)
data.sensitivity: RMS 0.033 mJy (N Band 3), 0.05 mJy (M Band 3), 0.35 mJy (N Band 6), 0.25 mJy (M Band 6)

what.value: Lower-resolution ALMA Band 3 catalog and image of Sgr B2 (project 2013.1.00269.S) used for photometry, fragmentation and stellar-mass comparison

evidence.quote: (cite: Ginsburg2018) obtained Band 3 observations of the extended Sgr B2 cloud at

what.value: Catalogs of known HII regions cross-matched to remove compact regions from the core sample

evidence.quote: In addition, we cross-match our detections with (cite: DePree1998) and (cite: Meng2022) to remove known compact regions from our core sample and label them as known regions.

what.value: Dust opacity models (kappa at 92 and 226 GHz) extrapolated as a power law with beta_dust = 1.75

evidence.quote: Extrapolating the (cite: Ossenkopf1994) opacity models for dust grains with thin ice mantles
as a power law, assuming $\beta_{\text{dust}} = 1.75$, we obtain $\kappa_{92 GHz} = 0.0017\ \frac{cm^2}{g}$ and $\kappa_{226 GHz} = 0.0083\ \frac{cm^2}{g}$

what.value: Average gas column density of Sgr B2 N and M clusters (~3e24 cm^-2) used in the optically-thick-core-in-dust model

evidence.quote: with an average over the Sgr B2 N and M cluster of around $3\times10^{24}$ $\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ (cite: Sanchez-Monge2017)

what.value: Kroupa initial mass function used to extrapolate the low-mass end for inferred stellar mass

evidence.quote: extrapolate the low-mass end of the Kroupa initial mass function (cite: Kroupa2001) to obtain the core-based inferred stellar mass

what.value: Star-forming age of the cloud, 0.74 Myr, used for the star formation rate

evidence.quote: Taking the star-forming age of the cloud as 0.74 Myr (cite: Kruijssen2015), we estimate the star formation rate (SFR) for each cluster.

what.value: Roughly one third of a core mass ends up in a star

evidence.quote: We further assume that roughly one third of a core mass will end up in a star (cite: Lada2003).

what.value: Disk dust-to-stellar mass ratio of ~1% extrapolated to more massive objects

evidence.quote: We extrapolate the ratio of the dust mass and the central star of $\sim$1% (cite: Williams2011) one order of magnitude for more massive objects

recipe.goal: Image and self-calibrate the four pointings
recipe.method: tclean imaging with iterative masked cleaning interleaved with phase then amplitude+phase self-calibration
key_parameters: Phase self-cal solint inf, then solint int, then phase+amp solint inf
Sgr B2 N Band 6: cleaning threshold raised to 10 sigma until amplitude self-cal, then extra phase+amplitude step with solint 15 s

recipe.goal: Check line contribution to the continuum
recipe.method: Extract spectra at core peak pixels in Sgr B2 N cubes, sigma-clip lines, compare mean before and after line removal
Noise measured in 30 concentric annuli with 7-sigma clipping, then a separate astrodendro run per annulus on the primary-beam-corrected image
key_parameters: min_value = 4 x noise, min_delta = 0.7 x noise, min_npix = 3 pixels

recipe.goal: Vet sources and build the core catalog
recipe.method: Manual exclusion polygons around extended emission, cross-match with known HII region catalogs, by-eye scoring 0/1/2 using 1 mm and 3 mm morphology, spectral index map
key_parameters: Score 1 and 2 both kept (complete catalog); robust and complete catalogs gave no significant difference
assumptions: A 3 mm filamentary structure without a 1 mm counterpart indicates free-free emission

recipe.method: Integrated flux within the dendrogram leaf contour and brightest pixel; peak-to-contour flux ratio used to judge whether a source is resolved
key_parameters: Aperture correction factor 1.465 for a 1-sigma aperture (used to compare with G18); frequency correction ~0.92
assumptions: Optically thick part of the core with spectral index of two for the G18 frequency correction

recipe.goal: Derive 3 mm to 1 mm spectral indexes
recipe.method: Band 6 convolved to the Band 3 beam; brightest-pixel fluxes at 3 mm positions compared at both bands; limits for single-band detections
key_parameters: Errors only for sources with SNR > 10 in both bands; all catalog sources SNR > 4

recipe.goal: Compute lower-limit core masses and fit the core mass function
recipe.method: Optically thin modified blackbody in the Rayleigh-Jeans limit, M = T_B d^2 / (kappa T_KE), applied to total dendrogram leaf flux with aperture correction; power law fit above completeness limit
key_parameters: Distance 8.4 kpc; 8.127 kpc would give 7% lower masses
Dust opacity kappa(92 GHz) = 0.0017 cm^2/g, kappa(226 GHz) = 0.0083 cm^2/g, beta_dust = 1.75
Completeness threshold 6 sigma (13.5 Msun); also 8 sigma (18 Msun)
assumptions: Dust optically thin (so masses are lower limits); 3 mm masses adopted as lower limits

recipe.goal: Test the nature of the sources (Stage 0/I vs other options)
recipe.method: Simple model of an optically thick sphere inside optically thin dust for expected spectral indexes; Stromgren-sphere test for HII regions; free-fall time and Bonnor-Ebert mass for prestellar nature; mass extrapolation for Stage II
key_parameters: Average dust temperature 50 K, gas-to-dust ratio 100, gas column ~3e24 cm^-2
assumptions: Magnetic fields do not contribute to core collapse support

recipe.goal: Infer total stellar mass and star formation rate
recipe.method: Sum core masses above completeness limit within cluster radii, extrapolate the Kroupa IMF down to 0.3 Msun, add HII regions at 45 Msun each, divide by cluster age
key_parameters: Cluster radii 0.4 pc (N) and 0.5 pc (M); 6 sigma completeness 0.3 mJy (M), 0.2 mJy (N); upper core limit 20 Msun
assumptions: One third of a core mass ends up in a star; each HII region powered by a >20 Msun star with IMF-weighted mean 45 Msun

recipe.goal: Quantify core fragmentation relative to the lower-resolution catalog
recipe.method: Count high-resolution detections within 1.5 x beam FWHM of each G18 source centre
key_parameters: Excluded G18 sources not detectable at pointing edges

answer_key.quantity: Number of sources detected at 3 mm and 1 mm

evidence.quote: we detect 371 sources at 3 mm and 218 sources in the smaller field of view at 1 mm.

answer_key.quantity: Unique cores detected at at least one wavelength

evidence.quote: Thus, the total number of individual cores identified at at least one wavelength is 410.

answer_key.quantity: HII region census in the catalog

evidence.quote: In total, our catalog contains 17 known hyper-compact and ultra-compact regions, 16 region candidates, and 8 new hyper-compact regions.

answer_key.value: 0.033 / 0.05 / 0.35 / 0.25 (N Band 3 / M Band 3 / N Band 6 / M Band 6)

evidence.quote: is 0.033 mJy for N Band 3, 0.05 mJy for M Band 3, 0.35 mJy for N Band 6, and 0.25 mJy for M Band 6.

answer_key.quantity: Mean relative line contribution to continuum

evidence.quote: We find that the mean relative line contribution for all cores is $-4.4\%$ for Band 3 and $-1.2\%$ for Band 6.

answer_key.quantity: Core mass function power-law slope above 6 sigma completeness (191 sources)

evidence.quote: The resulting fit of 191 sources is $\alpha = 2.4\pm 0.1$, which is consistent with the Kroupa IMF $\alpha = 2.35$.

answer_key.quantity: Core mass function power-law slope above 8 sigma (144 sources)

evidence.quote: the 144 sources produce a slightly steeper fit $\alpha = 2.6\pm 0.1$.

answer_key.quantity: Inferred stellar mass and SFR, Sgr B2 N

evidence.quote: We report source-counting-based inferred stellar mass and the star formation rate of the cloud: 2800M$_\odot$, 0.0038M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ for Sgr B2 N and 6900M$_\odot$, 0.0093M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ for Sgr B2 M respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Inferred stellar mass and SFR, Sgr B2 M

evidence.quote: We report source-counting-based inferred stellar mass and the star formation rate of the cloud: 2800M$_\odot$, 0.0038M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ for Sgr B2 N and 6900M$_\odot$, 0.0093M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ for Sgr B2 M respectively.
The resulting star formation rate is 0.0038M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ for Sgr B2 N and 0.0093M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ for Sgr B2 M totalling 0.013M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$

answer_key.quantity: Average number of cores per low-resolution (G18) source

evidence.quote: On average, each detected G18 source fragments into 2 cores.

answer_key.quantity: Average cores per fragmenting G18 source

evidence.quote: then there is an average of 3.4 cores per G18 fragmenting source.

answer_key.quantity: G18 sources detectable and detected at high resolution

evidence.quote: Of the 94 potentially detectable G18 sources, only 77 are detected at high-resolution.

answer_key.quantity: Spectral index range of most sources

evidence.quote: We find most sources to be marginally resolved and have a spectral index consistent with ${2<\alpha\lesssim3}$.
We calculate the aperture correction factor as the fraction of the Gaussian distribution that is cut off after using a 1-$\sigma$-sized aperture to be 1.465.
